headline: FrontierCS 2 benchmarks whether coding agents can improve real computer-science research artifacts
summary: An Oct 21 preprint introduces FrontierCS 2, a benchmark in which coding agents work inside real research repositories after the paper's contribution is removed, with the original implementation serving as the reference. A separate judge returns development feedback while withholding its evaluator and held-out workloads; a pass requires beating the reference on every metric and workload. The authors report 12 evaluated model-and-harness systems, one run per task across 48 public tasks and 13 computer-science domains. Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code passed 58% of its runs; no agent passed on 16 tasks. The author repository says 48 of 150 planned tasks are public and lists 13 model entries, including Kimi K2.7 as the FCI zero point. These are benchmark-author results, not independent evidence of general research capability; model and harness effects are paired.
